why: A method called through Function.prototype.apply or call is the direct call on its `this` (ECMA-262 20.2.3.1, 20.2.3.3; design/push-apply.md): common.mjs normaliseApplyCalls rewrites it before the lint and the translator read the file, so every analysis that knows a mutator by its callee sees the direct call. appendAll (push through apply), appendOne (push through call), front (unshift through apply), cut (splice through call), field (a record field as the receiver), local (a local array) and borrowed (Array.prototype.push applied to an array is that array's push) are the direct calls on the candidate: proved. dropped: the parent changes the parameter `a` only through apply and the candidate drops the call; the parent's Dafny returns `a` as an output and the candidate's does not, so the lemma is withheld as an interface difference (the scratch reading that left `a` out of syntacticMutations would have proved it); lane B: WITNESS. changed: push against unshift through call: refuted. count untouched: proved. A borrowed method whose `this` is not a plain path to an array, a list that is not a non-nullable array, and a bound value stay refused (fixtures/escapes/ts/push_apply.ts, library_members_push_apply.ts).
